newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes higher on soybean rally, showers.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes higher on soybean rally, showers.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on a rally in soybeans and on rain forecast for portions of the U.S. Midwest this week which may hamper corn seedings, traders said.
USDA Monday said as of Sunday, 18 percent of the U.S. crop had been planted, below trade expectations for 20 to 25 percent.

The rain that moved into the Midwest Tuesday night and overspread the western Corn Belt Wednesday is expected to be followed by another system on Friday. The precipitation was expected to further stall seeding.
Slow farm sales and firm basis also were supportive.
Nearby months gained on the deferreds on the strong rally in the soy complex. Tight soybean U.S. stocks amid active exports and soy crushings continued to boost soybean futures.

May corn futures rallied despite the posting Wednesday of 415,000 bushels of corn for possible delivery on the May. The market was not expecting any corn to be posted for delivery. Wednesday was first notice day for deliveries on the May.
Corn closed unchanged to 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with May up 3-1/2 at $2.95 a bushel. New crop December closed 3/4 cent higher at $2.75-1/2.

In spread trading, Continental Grain bull spread 13.0 million bushels of May/July at 1/2 to 3/4 cent, premium May, ADM Investor Services did two million May/July at 1/2 to 3/4 cent, and Continental did two million July/December at 16 cents, premium July, traders said.

Continental Grain bought five million bushels of July and sold three million bushels of December, traders said. FIMAT Futures bought three million December and bought two million bushels of July, traders said. Funds bought at least 10.0 million bushels of corn on the day, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 100,000 contracts, above the 96,520 traded Tuesday.

In corn options, LIT America sold 500 July $3.10 calls at five cents, Smith Barney bought 400 July $3.10 calls at five cents and ABN Amro-Chicago Corp sold 475 December $3.20 calls at eight cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, above the 13,199 traded Tuesday.
